query: Current official 2022-2026 European clinical practice guidelines for cancer of unknown primary, testicular cancer, penile cancer, and rare genitourinary cancers; prioritize ESMO, EAU, EURACAN and DOI or PubMed links
response:
## Findings

The authoritative European guidance published or maintained during 2022–2026 is principally:

1. **Cancer of unknown primary:** 2023 ESMO guideline.
2. **Testicular germ-cell cancer:** 2022 ESMO–EURACAN guideline plus the continuously maintained EAU guideline.
3. **Penile cancer:** 2023 EAU–ASCO collaborative guideline, current EAU online guideline, and 2024 ESMO–EURACAN guideline.
4. **Rare genitourinary cancers:** there is no single comprehensive ESMO/EAU document covering every rare GU malignancy; EURACAN organizes these through its **G9 rare urogenital tumours** domain, with disease-specific guidance—especially for penile, testicular and primary urethral cancers. [EURACAN G9](https://www.euracan.eu/domains/g9-rare-urogenital-tumours/) · [EAU guideline collection](https://uroweb.org/guidelines)

“Primary” below means the issuing society’s guideline page or the original guideline publication. PubMed is listed as a bibliographic/indexing source, not as the source of the recommendations.

---

## 1. Cancer of unknown primary — CUP

### Current core European guideline

**Krämer A, et al. Cancer of unknown primary: ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up.** *Annals of Oncology*. 2023;34(3):228–246. Published online 20 December 2022. DOI: **10.1016/j.annonc.2022.11.013**. The guideline addresses diagnostic work-up, CUP classification and risk assessment, favourable and unfavourable subsets, systemic and site-directed treatment, molecular testing, and follow-up.  
**Primary:** [ESMO guideline page](https://www.esmo.org/guidelines/esmo-clinical-practice-guideline-cancers-of-unknown-primary-site) · [Annals of Oncology full text](https://www.annalsofoncology.org/article/S0923-7534(22)04769-X/fulltext) · [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.annonc.2022.11.013)  
**Index:** [PubMed PMID 36563965](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36563965/)

This supersedes the older 2015 ESMO CUP guideline for current European practice. The 2023 paper is the relevant guideline within the requested 2022–2026 interval. [ESMO](https://www.esmo.org/guidelines/esmo-clinical-practice-guideline-cancers-of-unknown-primary-site) · [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36563965/)

---

## 2. Testicular cancer

### ESMO–EURACAN

**Oldenburg J, et al. Testicular seminoma and non-seminoma: ESMO–EURACAN Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up.** *Annals of Oncology*. 2022;33(4):362–375. DOI: **10.1016/j.annonc.2022.01.002**. This is the principal ESMO–EURACAN guideline for testicular germ-cell tumours in the requested period.  
**Primary:** [DOI/publisher](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.annonc.2022.01.002)  
**Index:** [PubMed title search](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=%22Testicular+seminoma+and+non-seminoma%3A+ESMO-EURACAN+Clinical+Practice+Guideline%22)

### EAU

The **EAU Guidelines on Testicular Cancer** are maintained as an online, periodically updated guideline. They cover diagnosis and staging, stage I surveillance and adjuvant options, metastatic seminoma and non-seminoma, residual masses, relapse, survivorship and follow-up. The live EAU page should be used to identify the edition currently in force rather than relying on an older downloaded PDF.  
**Primary:** [EAU Guidelines on Testicular Cancer](https://uroweb.org/guidelines/testicular-cancer)

### Practical status

For European practice, the ESMO–EURACAN publication and the live EAU guideline are complementary authoritative sources. ESMO–EURACAN is a fixed peer-reviewed 2022 publication, whereas EAU maintains a current online version and accompanying evidence summaries. [ESMO–EURACAN DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.annonc.2022.01.002) · [EAU](https://uroweb.org/guidelines/testicular-cancer)

---

## 3. Penile cancer

### EAU–ASCO collaborative guideline

**Brouwer OR, et al. European Association of Urology–American Society of Clinical Oncology Collaborative Guideline on Penile Cancer: 2023 Update.** *European Urology*. 2023;83(6):548–560. DOI: **10.1016/j.eururo.2023.02.027**. This is the peer-reviewed publication of the 2023 multidisciplinary EAU–ASCO recommendations.  
**Primary:** [DOI/publisher](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eururo.2023.02.027)  
**Index:** [PubMed title search](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=%22European+Association+of+Urology-American+Society+of+Clinical+Oncology+Collaborative+Guideline+on+Penile+Cancer%22)

The corresponding live EAU guideline covers primary-tumour management, inguinal and pelvic nodal staging and treatment, systemic therapy, surveillance, quality of life and centralization of care.  
**Primary:** [EAU Guidelines on Penile Cancer](https://uroweb.org/guidelines/penile-cancer)

### ESMO–EURACAN

**Penile cancer: ESMO–EURACAN Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up.** *ESMO Open*. 2024;9(7):103529. DOI: **10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.103529**. This provides the more recent ESMO–EURACAN multidisciplinary guidance and is particularly relevant for systemic treatment and advanced disease.  
**Primary:** [DOI/publisher](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.103529)  
**Index:** [PubMed title search](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=%22Penile+cancer%3A+ESMO-EURACAN+Clinical+Practice+Guideline%22)

### Practical status

For penile cancer, the strongest current European source set is the **live EAU guideline**, the **2023 EAU–ASCO peer-reviewed update**, and the **2024 ESMO–EURACAN guideline**. They are complementary rather than mutually exclusive. [EAU](https://uroweb.org/guidelines/penile-cancer) · [EAU–ASCO DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eururo.2023.02.027) · [ESMO–EURACAN DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.103529)

---

## 4. Rare genitourinary cancers

### Scope problem

“Rare genitourinary cancers” is not one histological or anatomical entity, and there is no single current ESMO/EAU guideline covering all rare GU malignancies. EURACAN groups them within **G9—Rare Urogenital Tumours**, while EAU and ESMO issue entity-specific guidance.  
**Primary organizational sources:** [EURACAN G9](https://www.euracan.eu/domains/g9-rare-urogenital-tumours/) · [EAU guideline collection](https://uroweb.org/guidelines)

### Primary urethral carcinoma

EAU maintains a dedicated **Guideline on Primary Urethral Carcinoma**, covering diagnostic evaluation, staging, localized male and female disease, regional lymph nodes, advanced disease and surveillance. Because the online guideline is updated, the live page should be used for the current edition.  
**Primary:** [EAU Guidelines on Primary Urethral Carcinoma](https://uroweb.org/guidelines/primary-urethral-carcinoma)

This ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline provides key recommendations for managing cancer of unknown primary (CUP).
The guideline covers CUP diagnosis, risk assessment, classification, treatment and follow-up.
Differential diagnostic algorithms for discrimination between CUP and other cancers are provided.
The author group includes multidisciplinary experts from different institutions in Europe, Australia and the United States.
Recommendations are based on available scientific data and the authors’ collective expert opinion.
In clinical practice, all recommendations provided need to be discussed with patients in a shared decision-making approach. Copyright © 2023 The European Society for Medical Oncology

citations.title: A Challenging Task: Identifying Patients with Cancer of Unknown Primary (CUP) According to ESMO Guidelines: The CUPISCO Trial Experience
citations.snippet: Background: CUPISCO is an ongoing randomized phase II trial ( NCT03498521 ) comparing molecularly guided therapy versus platinum-based chemotherapy in patients newly diagnosed with "unfavorable" cancer of unknown primary (CUP). Materials and methods: Patients with an unfavorable CUP diagnosis, as defined by the European Society of Medical Oncology (ESMO), and available cancer tissue for molecular sequencing are generally eligible. Potential patients with CUP entering screening undergo a review involving reference histopathology and clinical work-up by a central eligibility review team (ERT). Patients with "favorable" CUP, a strongly suspected primary site of origin, lack of tissue, or unmet inclusion criteria are excluded. A Challenging Task: Identifying Patients with Cancer of Unknown

This ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline provides key recommendations for managing cancer of unknown primary (CUP).
The guideline covers CUP diagnosis, risk assessment, classification, treatment and follow-up.
Differential diagnostic algorithms for discrimination between CUP and other cancers are provided.
The author group includes multidisciplinary experts from different institutions in Europe, Australia and the United States.
Recommendations are based on available scientific data and the authors’ collective expert opinion.
In clinical practice, all recommendations provided need to be discussed with patients in a shared decision-making approach. Copyright © 2023 The European Society for Medical Oncology

sources.title: A Challenging Task: Identifying Patients with Cancer of Unknown Primary (CUP) According to ESMO Guidelines: The CUPISCO Trial Experience
sources.snippet: Background: CUPISCO is an ongoing randomized phase II trial ( NCT03498521 ) comparing molecularly guided therapy versus platinum-based chemotherapy in patients newly diagnosed with "unfavorable" cancer of unknown primary (CUP). Materials and methods: Patients with an unfavorable CUP diagnosis, as defined by the European Society of Medical Oncology (ESMO), and available cancer tissue for molecular sequencing are generally eligible. Potential patients with CUP entering screening undergo a review involving reference histopathology and clinical work-up by a central eligibility review team (ERT). Patients with "favorable" CUP, a strongly suspected primary site of origin, lack of tissue, or unmet inclusion criteria are excluded. A Challenging Task: Identifying Patients with Cancer of Unknown

Challenges in the management of CUP include difficulties obtaining sufficient tissue for molecular profiling, and limited research opportunities due to the heterogeneity of CUP tumours. query: Current official 2022-2026 European guidelines for primary cutaneous lymphoma, lymphoma and myeloma; prioritize ESMO, EORTC, EHA and DOI or PubMed links
Current official 2022-2026 EANO ESTRO European guidelines for rare adult CNS tumours, meningioma, glioma and brain radiotherapy
response:
## Current EANO/ESTRO guideline set

The official starting point is the [EANO guideline catalogue](https://www.eano.eu/publications/eano-guidelines). The journal publications below are the **primary guideline sources**; organizational listings and later reviews are secondary sources.

### 1. Rare adult primary CNS tumours

#### EANO–EURACAN–SNO guideline for circumscribed astrocytic, glioneuronal and neuronal tumours — 2022
- **Citation:** Rudà R, et al. *EANO–EURACAN–SNO Guidelines on circumscribed astrocytic gliomas, glioneuronal, and neuronal tumors.* **Neuro-Oncology. 2022;24(12):2015–2034.**  
  [Primary guideline – DOI](https://doi.org/10.1093/neuonc/noac188)
- **Scope:** Rare adult and paediatric-type tumours encountered in adults, including pilocytic and high-grade astrocytoma with piloid features, pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma, subependymal giant-cell astrocytoma, chordoid glioma, astroblastoma and multiple glioneuronal/neuronal entities. It addresses integrated diagnosis, surgery, radiotherapy, systemic treatment and surveillance [primary guideline](https://doi.org/10.1093/neuonc/noac188).
- **Important limitation:** Recommendations are frequently based on retrospective series or expert consensus because prospective trials are scarce in these rare entities [primary guideline](https://doi.org/10.1093/neuonc/noac188).

This is the principal 2022–2026 EANO document matching “rare adult CNS tumours.” Separate older EANO/EURACAN documents exist for entities such as adult medulloblastoma and ependymal tumours, but they pre-date the requested interval and should not be presented as new 2022–2026 guidance.

---

### 2. Meningioma

#### Current comprehensive EANO meningioma guideline — published 2021, still the official core guideline
- **Citation:** Goldbrunner R, et al. *EANO guideline on the diagnosis and management of meningiomas.* **Neuro-Oncology. 2021;23(11):1821–1834.**  
  [Primary guideline – DOI](https://doi.org/10.1093/neuonc/noab150) | [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34181733/)
- **Status:** This falls just outside a strict 2022–2026 date filter, but it remains the current comprehensive EANO meningioma guideline listed and cited in current practice; I found no newer comprehensive EANO–ESTRO replacement in the official catalogue [EANO catalogue](https://www.eano.eu/publications/eano-guidelines).
- **Core framework:** Observation is appropriate for many incidental, asymptomatic tumours; surgery is generally the first option for growing or symptomatic disease; radiosurgery or fractionated radiotherapy may be used for selected inoperable, residual or recurrent tumours, while higher-grade disease generally requires more aggressive local management [primary guideline](https://doi.org/10.1093/neuonc/noab150).

#### Joint molecular-imaging/theranostics standard — 2024
A joint **EANM/EANO/RANO/SNMMI** practice guideline was published in 2024 for diagnosis and therapy of meningiomas using radiolabelled somatostatin-receptor ligands. It is a specialised nuclear-medicine procedure standard—not a replacement for the comprehensive 2021 clinical guideline. Its existence and publication details are documented in the 2025 *Journal of Nuclear Medicine* overview, which is a **secondary source**: [JNM full text/PDF](https://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/jnumed/66/1/24.full-text.pdf).

#### Not an EANO/ESTRO guideline
The 2023 ANOCEF target-volume consensus is useful European literature but was produced by the French ANOCEF group, not jointly by EANO and ESTRO: [primary ANOCEF consensus publication](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13014-023-02300-w).

---

### 3. Adult diffuse glioma: comprehensive clinical management

#### Current comprehensive EANO adult diffuse-glioma guideline — published 2020/2021
- **Citation:** Weller M, et al. *EANO guidelines on the diagnosis and treatment of diffuse gliomas of adulthood.* **Nature Reviews Clinical Oncology. 2021;18:170–186.**  
  [Primary guideline – DOI](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41571-020-00447-z)
- **Status:** Like the meningioma guideline, this predates 2022 but remains the principal comprehensive EANO document for diagnosis and multidisciplinary treatment. The newer ESTRO–EANO publications below supplement it specifically for radiotherapy planning; they do not replace all of its surgical, pathological and systemic-therapy recommendations [EANO catalogue](https://www.eano.eu/publications/eano-guidelines).

#### EANO molecular-testing guideline — 2023
- **Citation:** Capper D, et al. *EANO guideline on rational molecular testing of gliomas, glioneuronal, and neuronal tumors in adults for targeted therapy selection.* **Neuro-Oncology. 2023.**  
  [Primary guideline – DOI](https://doi.org/10.1093/neuonc/noad008)
- **Scope:** Provides a framework for selecting molecular tests when the result could establish a diagnosis, carry prognostic significance or support access to an approved or investigational targeted treatment [primary guideline](https://doi.org/10.1093/neuonc/noad008).
- This is a molecular-testing/precision-oncology guideline, not a complete treatment guideline.

---

### 4. Glioblastoma radiotherapy

#### ESTRO–EANO target-delineation and radiotherapy guideline — 2023
- **Citation:** Niyazi M, et al. *ESTRO–EANO guideline on target delineation and radiotherapy details for glioblastoma.* **Radiotherapy and Oncology. 2023;184:109663.**  
  [Primary guideline – DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.radonc.2023.109663) | [Official EANO listing](https://www.eano.eu/publications/eano-guidelines)
- **Scope:** Postoperative imaging, gross and clinical target-volume construction, anatomical editing, organs at risk, planning techniques, dose/fractionation and special clinical situations in adult glioblastoma [primary guideline](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.radonc.2023.109663).
- The standard planning framework uses the resection cavity and residual enhancing tumour as central components of the gross target, with incorporation of relevant non-enhancing disease and an anatomically adapted clinical-target margin; standard conventionally fractionated treatment remains approximately 60 Gy in 30 fractions for appropriate patients [primary guideline](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.radonc.2023.109663).

This is the most relevant current official European document for **glioblastoma brain-radiotherapy contouring**.

---

### 5. IDH-mutant WHO grade 2 and 3 diffuse glioma radiotherapy

#### ESTRO–EANO guideline — online 2024, journal issue 2025
- **Citation:** Baumert BG, et al. *ESTRO–EANO guideline on target delineation and radiotherapy for IDH-mutant WHO CNS grade 2 and 3 diffuse glioma.* **Radiotherapy and Oncology. 2025;202:110594.**  
  [Primary guideline – DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.radonc.2024.110594) | [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39454886/)
- **Date clarification:** The DOI and online publication are from 2024, while the assigned journal volume is 2025; either date may appear in bibliographies [primary publication](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.radonc.2024.110594).
- **Scope:** Radiotherapy indications and technical planning for adult **IDH-mutant astrocytoma and oligodendroglioma, CNS WHO grades 2–3**, using the WHO CNS5 classification [primary guideline](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.radonc.2024.110594).
- The guideline differentiates target margins and prescription according to grade; its standard schedules include approximately **50.4 Gy in 28 fractions for grade 2** and **59.4 Gy in 33 fractions for grade 3**, subject to the clinical scenario and normal-tissue constraints [primary guideline](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.radonc.2024.110594).

This complements, rather than replaces, the broader EANO diffuse-glioma clinical guideline.

---

## Practical authoritative hierarchy

| Topic | Current core document | Publication date | Classification |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Rare circumscribed/glioneuronal/neuronal CNS tumours

citations.title: EANO guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of meningiomas. - Abstract - Europe PMC
citations.snippet:
Although meningiomas are the most common intracranial tumours, the level of evidence to provide recommendations for the diagnosis and treatment of meningiomas is low compared with other tumours such as high-grade gliomas. The meningioma task force of the European Association of Neuro-Oncology (EANO) assessed the scientific literature and composed a framework of the best possible evidence-based recommendations for health professionals. The provisional diagnosis of meningioma is mainly made by MRI. Definitive diagnosis, including histological classification, grading, and molecular profiling, requires a surgical procedure to obtain tumour tissue. Therefore, in many elderly patients, observation is the best therapeutic option. Full text links

sources.title: EANO guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of meningiomas. - Abstract - Europe PMC
sources.snippet:
Although meningiomas are the most common intracranial tumours, the level of evidence to provide recommendations for the diagnosis and treatment of meningiomas is low compared with other tumours such as high-grade gliomas. The meningioma task force of the European Association of Neuro-Oncology (EANO) assessed the scientific literature and composed a framework of the best possible evidence-based recommendations for health professionals. The provisional diagnosis of meningioma is mainly made by MRI. Definitive diagnosis, including histological classification, grading, and molecular profiling, requires a surgical procedure to obtain tumour tissue. Therefore, in many elderly patients, observation is the best therapeutic option. Full text links

query: Current official 2022-2026 European guidelines for neuroendocrine tumours; prioritize ESMO and ENETS with DOI or PubMed links
response:
## Scope and source hierarchy

As of **March 2026**, the principal European society sources for neuroendocrine neoplasms are:

1. **ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines** — formal multidisciplinary clinical-practice guidelines.
2. **ENETS guidance papers** — official, expert-led, question-based recommendations, generally organized by primary site or clinical syndrome. ENETS describes these papers as addressing specific clinical-management questions rather than constituting one omnibus guideline. [ESMO guideline portal](https://www.esmo.org/guidelines/esmo-clinical-practice-guidelines-endocrine-and-neuroendocrine-cancers); [ENETS official guideline index](https://www.enets.org/guidelines.html)

The publications below are therefore **primary guidance sources**. Reviews comparing guidelines are secondary sources and should not override the underlying ESMO or ENETS documents.

---

## 1. ESMO: current in-window guideline

### Gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms — 2024

**Pavel M, et al. Gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms: ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up.** *ESMO Open*. 2024;9(10):103664.

- Covers gastroenteropancreatic well-differentiated NETs and poorly differentiated NECs, including diagnosis, staging, surgery, systemic treatment, radionuclide therapy and follow-up.
- This is the principal in-window ESMO guideline for GEP-NEN and updates ESMO’s earlier 2020 publication.
- **DOI:** [10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.103664](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.103664)
- **Official ESMO page:** [ESMO GEP-NEN Clinical Practice Guideline](https://www.esmo.org/guidelines/esmo-clinical-practice-guideline-gastroenteropancreatic-neuroendocrine-neoplasms)
- **PubMed search:** [Pavel 2024 ESMO GEP-NEN guideline](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=%22Gastroenteropancreatic+neuroendocrine+neoplasms%22+%22103664%22)

ESMO’s broader endocrine/neuroendocrine portal also includes site-specific guidance for entities such as lung/thymic carcinoids and other endocrine cancers, but some of those documents predate the requested 2022–2026 publication window. [ESMO endocrine and neuroendocrine guideline portal](https://www.esmo.org/guidelines/esmo-clinical-practice-guidelines-endocrine-and-neuroendocrine-cancers)

---

## 2. ENETS official guidance, 2022–2025

### A. Carcinoid syndrome and carcinoid heart disease — 2022

**European Neuroendocrine Tumor Society (ENETS) 2022 Guidance Paper for Carcinoid Syndrome and Carcinoid Heart Disease.** *Journal of Neuroendocrinology*. 2022.

- Dedicated guidance on recognition and treatment of carcinoid syndrome, biochemical assessment, refractory syndrome, screening for carcinoid heart disease and multidisciplinary cardiac management.
- **DOI:** [10.1111/jne.13146](https://doi.org/10.1111/jne.13146)
- **PubMed:** [Title search](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=%22ENETS+2022+Guidance+Paper+for+Carcinoid+Syndrome+and+Carcinoid+Heart+Disease%22)

### B. Digestive neuroendocrine carcinoma — 2023

**Sorbye H, Grande E, Pavel M, et al. European Neuroendocrine Tumor Society (ENETS) 2023 guidance paper for digestive neuroendocrine carcinoma.** *Journal of Neuroendocrinology*. 2023;35(3):e13249.

- Addresses poorly differentiated digestive NEC, which should not be managed as if it were a well-differentiated NET.
- **DOI:** [10.1111/jne.13249](https://doi.org/10.1111/jne.13249)
- **PubMed:** [Title search](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=%22ENETS+2023+guidance+paper+for+digestive+neuroendocrine+carcinoma%22)

### C. Appendiceal neuroendocrine tumours — 2023

**European Neuroendocrine Tumor Society (ENETS) 2023 guidance paper for appendiceal neuroendocrine tumours.** *Journal of Neuroendocrinology*. 2023.

- Site-specific recommendations concerning pathological risk assessment, indications for additional surgery after appendectomy, staging and surveillance.
- **PubMed:** [Exact-title search](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=%22European+Neuroendocrine+Tumor+Society%22+%222023+guidance+paper+for+appendiceal+neuroendocrine+tumours%22)
- **Official index:** [ENETS Guidelines & Standards of Care](https://www.enets.org/guidelines.html)

### D. Gastroduodenal neuroendocrine tumours — 2023

**European Neuroendocrine Tumor Society (ENETS) 2023 guidance paper for gastroduodenal neuroendocrine tumours.** *Journal of Neuroendocrinology*. 2023.

- Covers gastric and duodenal NET subtypes, endoscopic and surgical management, staging and surveillance.
- **PubMed:** [Exact-title search](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=%22ENETS+2023+guidance+paper+for+gastroduodenal+neuroendocrine+tumours%22)
- **Official index:** [ENETS Guidelines & Standards of Care](https://www.enets.org/guidelines.html)

### E. Colorectal neuroendocrine tumours — 2023

**European Neuroendocrine Tumor Society (ENETS) 2023 guidance paper for colorectal neuroendocrine tumours.** *Journal of Neuroendocrinology*. 2023.

- Addresses rectal and colonic NETs, including endoscopic versus surgical management and post-resection assessment.
- **PubMed:** [Exact-title search](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=%22ENETS+2023+guidance+paper+for+colorectal+neuroendocrine+tumours%22)
- **Official index:** [ENETS Guidelines & Standards of Care](https://www.enets.org/guidelines.html)

### F. Functioning pancreatic NET syndromes — 2023

**Hofland J, Falconi M, Christ E, et al. European Neuroendocrine Tumor Society 2023 guidance paper for functioning pancreatic neuroendocrine tumour syndromes.** *Journal of Neuroendocrinology*. 2023.

- Syndrome-specific guidance for functioning pancreatic NETs, including insulinoma, gastrinoma and rarer hormonal syndromes.
- **PubMed:** [Exact-title search](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=%22ENETS+2023+guidance+paper+for+functioning+pancreatic+neuroendocrine+tumour+syndromes%22)
- **Official index:** [ENETS Guidelines & Standards of Care](https://www.enets.org/guidelines.html)

### G. Nonfunctioning pancreatic NETs — 2023

**Kos-Kudła B, et al. European Neuroendocrine Tumour Society (ENETS) 2023 guidance paper for nonfunctioning pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours.** *Journal of Neuroendocrinology*. 2023.

- Covers incidental/localized nonfunctioning PanNETs, observation versus resection, staging, advanced disease and follow-up.
- **DOI:** [10.1111/jne.13343](https://doi.org/10.1111/jne.13343)
- **Publisher record:** [Wiley](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/jne.13343)
- **PubMed:** [Exact-title search](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=%22ENETS+2023+guidance+paper+for+nonfunctioning+pancreatic+neuroendocrine+tumours%22)

### H. Well-differentiated small-intestinal NETs — 2024

**Lamarca A, Bartsch DK, Caplin M, et al. European Neuroendocrine Tumor Society (ENETS) 2024 guidance paper for the management of well-differentiated small intestine neuroendocrine tumours.** *Journal of Neuroendocrinology*. 2024.

- Current ENETS site-specific guidance for

query: Current 2024-2026 French INCa and HAS recommendations for cancer epidemiology prevention screening and oncologic emergencies
response:
## Synthèse des recommandations françaises INCa–HAS applicables en 2024–2026

### Cadre et limites

- **Sources primaires** : publications de l’[Institut national du cancer — INCa](https://www.cancer.fr/) et de la [Haute Autorité de santé — HAS](https://www.has-sante.fr/). Le site de l’INCa a été renommé **cancer.fr**.
- **Sources secondaires** : sociétés savantes, réseaux régionaux et articles professionnels, utiles pour l’application clinique mais ne constituant pas, à eux seuls, une recommandation nationale INCa/HAS.
- Une recommandation publiée avant 2024 peut rester la recommandation nationale en vigueur si elle n’a pas été remplacée. Il ne faut donc pas interpréter « recommandations 2024–2026 » comme signifiant que tous les textes ont été réédités pendant cette période.
- Je n’ai pas identifié de **référentiel national INCa/HAS unique, publié en 2024–2026, couvrant toutes les urgences oncologiques**. Pour ce domaine, des référentiels de sociétés savantes et des protocoles locaux complètent les textes institutionnels.

---

# 1. Épidémiologie des cancers en France

Les estimations nationales de référence sont produites dans le cadre du partenariat **Francim–Hospices civils de Lyon–Santé publique France–INCa**, plutôt que par extrapolation à partir des seules données hospitalières. Les dernières estimations nationales consolidées font état d’environ **433 000 nouveaux cas de cancer en France métropolitaine en 2023** : environ 245 600 chez les hommes et 187 500 chez les femmes. Le cancer de la prostate est le plus fréquent chez l’homme et celui du sein chez la femme; les cancers colorectaux et pulmonaires figurent parmi les plus fréquents dans les deux sexes ([INCa, *Panorama des cancers en France 2024*](https://www.cancer.fr/professionnels-de-sante/les-chiffres-du-cancer-en-france/epidemiologie-des-cancers)).

L’incidence globale augmente notamment sous l’effet de la croissance et du vieillissement démographiques. Après standardisation sur l’âge, les évolutions diffèrent toutefois selon le sexe et la localisation; l’augmentation du cancer pulmonaire chez les femmes reflète en particulier l’évolution historique du tabagisme féminin ([INCa, épidémiologie des cancers](https://www.cancer.fr/professionnels-de-sante/les-chiffres-du-cancer-en-france/epidemiologie-des-cancers)).

Les données d’incidence les plus récentes et les données de mortalité ne portent pas nécessairement sur la même année, en raison des délais de consolidation des certificats de décès et des registres. Il faut donc toujours indiquer l’année de référence plutôt que de présenter incidence et mortalité comme des mesures contemporaines ([Santé publique France, cancers](https://www.santepubliquefrance.fr/maladies-et-traumatismes/cancers)).

---

# 2. Prévention primaire

## 2.1 Tabac

Le tabac demeure le **premier facteur de risque évitable de cancer** en France. Il est causalement associé, entre autres, aux cancers du poumon, des voies aérodigestives supérieures, de la vessie, du rein, du pancréas et du col utérin. L’objectif clinique prioritaire est l’absence d’initiation ou l’arrêt, quel que soit l’âge; le bénéfice de l’arrêt existe même après une consommation prolongée ([INCa, tabac et cancers](https://www.cancer.fr/toute-l-information-sur-les-cancers/prevenir-les-cancers/reduire-les-risques-de-cancer/tabac)).

La HAS recommande de rechercher régulièrement le statut tabagique, de conseiller explicitement l’arrêt, d’évaluer la dépendance et de proposer un accompagnement comportemental associé, si nécessaire, à un traitement pharmacologique. Les **substituts nicotiniques** constituent le traitement médicamenteux de première intention dans la stratégie HAS ([HAS, *Arrêt de la consommation de tabac*](https://www.has-sante.fr/jcms/c_1718021/fr/arret-de-la-consommation-de-tabac-du-depistage-individuel-au-maintien-de-l-abstinence-en-premier-recours)).

## 2.2 Alcool

La consommation d’alcool augmente le risque de plusieurs cancers, notamment ceux de la bouche, du pharynx, du larynx, de l’œsophage, du foie, du côlon-rectum et du sein. Du point de vue du risque de cancer, **il n’existe pas de consommation sans risque**; le risque augmente avec la quantité consommée ([INCa, alcool et cancers](https://www.cancer.fr/toute-l-information-sur-les-cancers/prevenir-les-cancers/reduire-les-risques-de-cancer/alcool)).

Les repères français destinés à réduire le risque sont : **pas plus de 10 verres standard par semaine, pas plus de 2 par jour et des jours sans consommation**. Ces repères relèvent de l’expertise Santé publique France–INCa et ne doivent pas être présentés comme un seuil de sécurité carcinologique ([Santé publique France, repères de consommation](https://www.santepubliquefrance.fr/determinants-de-sante/alcool/articles/quels-sont-les-risques-de-la-consommation-d-alcool-pour-la-sante)).

## 2.3 Nutrition, activité physique et poids

La prévention repose également sur :

- une activité physique régulière;
- la réduction de la sédentarité;
- le maintien d’un poids adapté;
- une alimentation riche en céréales complètes, légumes secs, fruits et légumes;
- la limitation des viandes rouges et surtout des charcuteries;
- la limitation des aliments très caloriques, boissons sucrées et excès de sel.

Ces mesures s’inscrivent dans les recommandations INCa fondées sur les expertises internationales concernant les relations entre nutrition et cancer ([INCa, nutrition et prévention](https://www.cancer.fr/toute-l-information-sur-les-cancers/prevenir-les-cancers/reduire-les-risques-de-cancer/alimentation)).

## 2.4 Expositions solaires et UV artificiels

L’INCa recommande d’éviter les coups de soleil, particulièrement pendant l’enfance, de rechercher l’ombre, de porter des vêtements protecteurs et de ne pas utiliser de cabines de bronzage. La crème solaire complète ces mesures mais ne doit pas servir à prolonger l’exposition ([INCa, rayonnements UV](https://www.cancer.fr/toute-l-information-sur-les-cancers/prevenir-les-cancers/reduire-les-risques-de-cancer/rayonnements-ultraviolets)).

## 2.5 Vaccination contre les HPV

La vaccination anti-HPV est recommandée en routine aux **filles et garçons de 11 à 14 ans**, avec rattrapage chez les personnes non vaccinées ou incomplètement vaccinées. La HAS a recommandé en 2024 d’étendre le rattrapage jusqu’à **26 ans révolus** chez les femmes comme chez les hommes; son application pratique doit être vérifiée dans le calendrier vaccinal national de l’année considérée ([HAS, extension du rattrapage vaccinal contre les HPV](https://www.has-sante.fr/jcms/p_3538462/fr/extension-de-la-vaccination-contre-les-papillomavirus-chez-les-jeunes-adultes-jusqu-a-26-ans), [Ministère de la Santé, calendrier vaccinal](https://sante.gouv.fr/prevention-en-sante/preserver-sa-sante/vaccination/calendrier-vaccinal)).

La vaccination ne remplace pas le dépistage du col de l’utérus, car elle ne couvre pas toutes les infections HPV oncogènes et ne traite pas une infection déjà constituée ([INCa, vaccination HPV](https://www.cancer.fr/toute-l-information-sur-les-cancers/prevenir-les-cancers/la-vaccination-contre-les-hpv)).

## 2.6 Hépatites et risques professionnels

La vaccination contre l’hépatite B participe à la prévention du carcinome hépatocellulaire en prévenant l’infection chronique. La prévention comprend aussi la réduction des expositions professionnelles à l’amiante, aux poussières de bois, au benzène, aux rayonnements ionisants et à d’autres cancérogènes, conformément à la réglementation et à l’évaluation du risque professionnel ([INCa, cancers liés au travail](https://www.cancer.fr/toute-l-information-sur-les-cancers/prevenir-les-cancers/reduire-les-risques-de-cancer/cancers-lies-au-travail)).

---

# 3. Dépistages recommandés

## 3.1 Cancer du sein : programme organisé

Le programme organisé concerne les femmes de **50 à 74 ans**, sans symptôme ni facteur de très haut risque justifiant une surveillance spécifique. Il prévoit une **mammographie tous les deux ans**, associée à un examen clinique des seins; les mammographies jugées normales bénéficient d’une seconde lecture dans le programme ([INCa, dépistage du cancer du sein](https://www.cancer.fr/toute-l-information-sur-les-cancers/se-faire-depister/depistage-du-cancer-du-sein)).

La HAS recommande l’introduction de la **tomosynthèse**, à condition qu’elle soit associée à la reconstruction d’une image 2D synthétique — combinaison **3D + 2Ds** — et non utilisée seule dans le dépistage organisé ([HAS, actualisation du dépistage organisé du cancer du sein](https://www.has-sante.fr/jcms/p_3421814/fr/la-has-actualise-ses-recommandations-sur-l-examen-du-depistage-organise-du-cancer-du-sein)).

Les femmes ayant un risque élevé ou très élevé — mutation prédisposante, antécédent d’irradiation thoracique à forte dose, antécédents personnels ou familiaux particuliers — relèvent d’une surveillance individualisée et non du seul calendrier standard ([HAS, dépistage selon le niveau de risque](https://www.has-sante.fr/jcms/c_1741170/fr/depistage-du-cancer-du-sein-en-france-identification-des-femmes-a-haut-risque-et-modalites-de-depistage)).

Il n’existe pas de recommandation française de dépistage mammographique organisé systématique avant 50 ans chez les femmes à risque moyen. Tout symptôme mammaire impose en revanche une démarche diagnostique, quel que soit l’âge, et non l’attente du prochain dépistage.

## 3.2 Cancer colorectal : programme organisé

Chez les personnes asymptomatiques de **50 à 74 ans à risque moyen**, le programme repose sur un **test immunologique fécal tous les deux ans**. Un résultat positif doit être suivi d’une coloscopie; le test positif ne constitue pas un diagnostic de cancer ([INCa, dépistage du cancer colorectal](https://www.cancer.fr/toute-l-information-sur-les-cancers/se-faire-depister/depistage-du-cancer-colorectal)).

Les personnes présentant des symptômes digestifs d’alarme, un antécédent personnel d’adénome ou de cancer colorectal, une maladie inflammatoire chronique intestinale ou un risque familial/génétique élevé ne relèvent pas du test fécal standard : elles nécessitent une évaluation diagnostique et/ou une surveillance coloscopique adaptée ([INCa, niveaux de risque colorectal](https://www.cancer.fr/toute-l-information-sur-les-cancers/se-faire-depister/depistage-du-cancer-colorectal/a-qui-s-adresse-le-depistage)).

## 3.3 Cancer du col de l’utérus : programme organisé

Le programme concerne les femmes asymptomatiques de **25 à 65 ans**, y compris celles vaccinées contre les HPV :

- **25–29 ans** : dépistage cytologique; deux examens à un an d’intervalle, puis un examen trois ans plus tard si les deux premiers sont normaux;
- **30–65 ans** : test HPV à haut risque, réalisé trois ans après la dernière cytologie normale puis, s’il est négatif, tous les cinq ans.

Ces intervalles correspondent à la stratégie HAS intégrée au programme national organisé ([HAS, évaluation du test HPV en dépistage primaire](https://www.has-sante.fr/jcms/c_2806160/fr/evaluation-de-la-recherche-des-papillomavirus-humains-hpv-en-depistage-primaire-des-lesions-precancereuses-et-cancereuses-du-col-de-l-uterus-et-de-la-place-du-double-immuno-marquage-p16/ki67), [INCa, dépistage du col de l’utérus](https://www.cancer.fr/toute-l-information-sur-les-cancers/se-faire-depister/depistage-du-cancer-du-col-de-l-uterus)).

Une cytologie ou un test HPV anormal relève des algorithmes INCa de triage, colposcopie, biopsie et suivi; un résultat HPV positif n’est pas synonyme de cancer. Les recommandations de conduite à tenir ont fait l’objet d’une actualisation INCa autour des anomalies cytologiques après test HPV positif; il faut utiliser la version décisionnelle la plus récente disponible sur cancer.fr plutôt qu’un ancien arbre isolé.

## 3.4 Cancer du poumon

La HAS a conclu que les données permettaient d’engager un **programme pilote** de dépistage par scanner thoracique à faible dose chez des personnes fortement exposées au tabac, mais elle n’a pas assimilé cette expérimentation à un programme national organisé généralisé ([HAS, dépistage du cancer broncho-pulmonaire](https://www.has-sante.fr/jcms/p_3312901/fr/cancer-du-poumon-la-has-recommande-l-engagement-d-un-programme-pilote-de-depistage)).

En pratique, en 2024–2026, il faut vérifier l’état du déploiement du pilote INCa et ses critères d’inclusion. Un scanner réalisé hors protocole ne doit pas être présenté comme le dépistage organisé national. Le dépistage, lorsqu’il est proposé, doit être couplé à une intervention de sevrage tabagique.

## 3.5 Prostate, peau, ovaire et autres cancers

Il n’existe pas en France de programme national organisé de dépistage du cancer de la prostate chez les hommes asymptomatiques à risque moyen. Le dosage du PSA peut entraîner surdiagnostic et surtraitement; toute démarche individuelle doit être précédée d’une information sur les bénéfices incertains et les risques ([HAS, dépistage du cancer de la prostate](https://www.has-sante.fr/jcms/c_1238318/fr/cancer-de-la-prostate-identification-des-facteurs-de-risque-et-pertinence-d-un-depistage-par-dosage-de-l-antigene-specifique-prostatique-psa-de-populations-d-hommes-a-haut-risque)).

Il n’existe pas non plus de dépistage organisé national du mélanome, du cancer de l’ovaire ou du cancer du pancréas dans la population générale asymptomatique. Les sujets présentant une prédisposition héréditaire ou un risque particulièrement élevé relèvent de filières spécialisées d’oncogénétique et de surveillance ciblée, et non d’un dépistage de masse ([INCa, détection précoce et dépistages](https://www.cancer.fr/toute-l-information-sur-les-cancers/se-faire-depister)).

---

citations.title: Haute Autorité de Santé - La HAS actualise ses recommandations sur l’examen du dépistage organisé du cancer du sein
citations.snippet: Le dépistage organisé, proposé tous les deux ans aux femmes âgées de 50 à 74 ans, permet leur détection et leur prise en charge précoces. En réponse à une saisine de l’Institut national du cancer (INCa), la Haute Autorité de santé recommande l’introduction, dans le dépistage organisé des cancers du sein, de la mammographie 3D (par tomosynthèse), à condition qu’elle soit systématiquement associée à la reconstruction d’une image 2D synthétique (3D + 2Ds). Depuis 2009 cette technique d’imagerie est largement utilisée en France en dehors du cadre du dépistage organisé, notamment chez des femmes à haut risque de cancer du sein ou dans le cadre de la surveillance d’un cancer diagnostiqué, où elle a démontré des résultats bénéfiques. citations.title: Indispensables: les nouvelles recommandations INCA sur la prise en charge des femmes ayant une cytologie cervico-utérine anormale après un test HPV positif
citations.snippet:
Photo du rédacteur: Sylvie Mesrine Sylvie Mesrine
17 mars 2025
1 min de lecture Indispensables: les nouvelles recommandations INCA sur la prise en charge des femmes ayant une cytologie cervico-utérine anormale après un test HPV positif Les recommandations de l’INCa sur la conduite à tenir devant une femme ayant une cytologie cervico-utérine anormale ont été publiées en 2016. En 2019, la Haute Autorité de santé (HAS) a recommandé le test HPV pour dépister le cancer du col chez les femmes de plus de 30 ans. L'INCA vient de présenter les nouvelles recommandations d'un consensus de 35 experts, sous forme de 17 arbres décisionnels:
13 sur la conduite diagnostique face aux différentes anomalies cytologiques, stratiﬁée selon l’âge top of page

sources.title: Haute Autorité de Santé - La HAS actualise ses recommandations sur l’examen du dépistage organisé du cancer du sein
sources.snippet: Le dépistage organisé, proposé tous les deux ans aux femmes âgées de 50 à 74 ans, permet leur détection et leur prise en charge précoces. En réponse à une saisine de l’Institut national du cancer (INCa), la Haute Autorité de santé recommande l’introduction, dans le dépistage organisé des cancers du sein, de la mammographie 3D (par tomosynthèse), à condition qu’elle soit systématiquement associée à la reconstruction d’une image 2D synthétique (3D + 2Ds). Depuis 2009 cette technique d’imagerie est largement utilisée en France en dehors du cadre du dépistage organisé, notamment chez des femmes à haut risque de cancer du sein ou dans le cadre de la surveillance d’un cancer diagnostiqué, où elle a démontré des résultats bénéfiques. L’Institut

sources.title: Indispensables: les nouvelles recommandations INCA sur la prise en charge des femmes ayant une cytologie cervico-utérine anormale après un test HPV positif
sources.snippet:
Photo du rédacteur: Sylvie Mesrine Sylvie Mesrine
17 mars 2025
1 min de lecture Indispensables: les nouvelles recommandations INCA sur la prise en charge des femmes ayant une cytologie cervico-utérine anormale après un test HPV positif Les recommandations de l’INCa sur la conduite à tenir devant une femme ayant une cytologie cervico-utérine anormale ont été publiées en 2016. En 2019, la Haute Autorité de santé (HAS) a recommandé le test HPV pour dépister le cancer du col chez les femmes de plus de 30 ans. L'INCA vient de présenter les nouvelles recommandations d'un consensus de 35 experts, sous forme de 17 arbres décisionnels:
13 sur la conduite diagnostique face aux différentes anomalies cytologiques, stratiﬁée selon l’âge top of page

query: Current official 2022-2026 European guidelines for rare head and neck cancers including salivary gland, nasopharyngeal cancer and sinonasal malignancies; prioritize ESMO EURACAN
response:
## Evidence summary

As of **March 2026**, the ESMO–EURACAN portfolio contains recent dedicated European guidelines for **salivary-gland cancer (2022)** and **sinonasal malignancy (2025)**. The latest dedicated ESMO–EURACAN guideline for **nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC)** appears to remain the **2021** publication; therefore, it falls just outside a strict 2022–2026 publication window but is still the relevant European ESMO–EURACAN document.

### Current primary guidelines

| Disease | Current ESMO/EURACAN document | Status and scope |
|---|---|---|
| **Salivary-gland cancer** | van Herpen C, et al. *Salivary gland cancer: ESMO–European Reference Network on Rare Adult Solid Cancers (EURACAN) Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up.* **ESMO Open. 2022;7(6):100602.** [DOI/full text](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.esmoop.2022.100602) · [Official ESMO page](https://www.esmo.org/guidelines/esmo-euracan-clinical-practice-guideline-salivary-gland-cancer) | **Primary guideline; within the requested period.** Covers major and minor salivary-gland carcinomas, pathology and molecular diagnosis, staging, surgery, radiotherapy, recurrent/metastatic disease, targeted therapy and follow-up.[Guideline](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.esmoop.2022.100602) |
| **Sinonasal malignancy** | Resteghini C, et al. *Sinonasal malignancy: ESMO–EURACAN Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up.* **ESMO Open. 2025;10(2):104121.** [DOI/full text](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.104121) · [Official ESMO page](https://www.esmo.org/guidelines/esmo-euracan-clinical-practice-guideline-sinonasal-malignancy) | **Primary guideline; newest of the three.** Published in the February 2025 issue despite a 2024 DOI suffix. It addresses epithelial sinonasal malignancies, including surgery, radiotherapy and particle therapy, and response-adapted use of neoadjuvant chemotherapy.[Publisher record](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2059702924018921) |
| **Nasopharyngeal carcinoma** | Bossi P, et al. *Nasopharyngeal carcinoma: ESMO–EURACAN Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up.* **Ann Oncol. 2021;32(4):452–465.** [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.annonc.2020.12.007) | **Primary European ESMO–EURACAN guideline, but outside the strict 2022–2026 window.** It remains the key dedicated European ESMO–EURACAN NPC guideline unless ESMO issues a newer replacement. Its scope includes diagnosis and staging, radiotherapy, combined-modality treatment, recurrent/metastatic disease and surveillance.[Guideline](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.annonc.2020.12.007) |

## Important scope qualifications

- The **2025 sinonasal guideline is not a single guideline for every tumour arising in the sinonasal tract**. Salivary-type malignancies, mesenchymal tumours and sinonasal mucosal melanoma were excluded because they are managed through other disease-specific frameworks.[Guideline bibliographic record](https://www.muni.cz/vyzkum/publikace/2488679)  
- Consequently, a sinonasal tumour with salivary-type histology may be better mapped to the **2022 salivary-gland guideline**, while sarcoma and mucosal melanoma require their respective ESMO/EURACAN disease guidelines.[Sinonasal scope](https://www.muni.cz/vyzkum/publikace/2488679)
- ESMO’s guideline landing pages are **official organizational records**, but the peer-reviewed guideline articles above are the **primary clinical sources** containing the full recommendations, evidence grading and algorithms.[ESMO salivary page](https://www.esmo.org/guidelines/esmo-euracan-clinical-practice-guideline-salivary-gland-cancer) [ESMO sinonasal page](https://www.esmo.org/guidelines/esmo-euracan-clinical-practice-guideline-sinonasal-malignancy)

## High-level clinical content

### Salivary-gland cancer

The 2022 guideline emphasizes expert pathological classification, appropriate cross-sectional imaging, surgery as the principal curative treatment for resectable disease, and risk-adapted postoperative radiotherapy. For recurrent or metastatic disease, histology and molecular characteristics—including actionable alterations or receptor expression in appropriate subtypes—are central to systemic-treatment selection.[van Herpen et al., 2022](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.esmoop.2022.100602)

### Sinonasal malignancy

The 2025 guideline emphasizes multidisciplinary management in experienced centres, expert pathology supported by molecular testing where diagnostically relevant, CT/MRI-based assessment, and complete surgical resection where feasible. It also discusses endoscopic versus open approaches, postoperative or definitive radiotherapy, potential advantages of particle therapy in selected anatomy, and neoadjuvant chemotherapy for selected high-grade or locally advanced tumours to inform organ-preserving locoregional treatment.[Resteghini et al., 2025](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.104121)

### Nasopharyngeal carcinoma

The 2021 ESMO–EURACAN guideline supports modern intensity-modulated radiotherapy as the locoregional treatment platform, stage- and risk-adapted integration of platinum-based chemotherapy, and systemic therapy for recurrent/metastatic disease. Because this document predates the requested period, any use for present-day prescribing should be checked against subsequent drug approvals, ESMO living recommendations and national reimbursement rules.[Bossi et al., 2021](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.annonc.2020.12.007)

## Primary versus secondary sources

**Use as primary authorities**

1. The three peer-reviewed ESMO–EURACAN guideline articles linked above.
2. Their official ESMO guideline landing pages.
3. Any subsequent ESMO correction, focused update or living-guideline notice attached to those pages.

**Secondary sources**

Medscape summaries, narrative reviews, institutional webpages and retrospective studies may be useful for orientation but should not replace the guideline text. For example, Medscape has summaries of the salivary and sinonasal recommendations, while later reviews cite the ESMO–EURACAN documents; these are derivative rather than issuing bodies.[Medscape salivary summary](https://reference.medscape.com/cc2/p10/guideline-essentials-2022-esmo-euracan-recommendations-2024a10003c5) [Medscape sinonasal summary](https://reference.medscape.com/cc2/p10/guideline-essentials-esmo-recommendations-diagnosis-and-2025a1000cup)

### Bottom line

For a European guideline set covering the requested diseases, the appropriate core is:

1. **Salivary gland — ESMO–EURACAN 2022**
2. **Sinonasal malignancy — ESMO–EURACAN 2025**
3. **Nasopharyngeal carcinoma — ESMO–EURACAN 2021**, explicitly documented as the latest dedicated European guideline found but outside the nominal 2022–2026 interval.

high-grade tumours including SCC, olfactory neuroblastoma (Hyams grade III–IV), sinonasal undifferentiated carcinoma, sinonasal neuroendocrine carcinoma, and small-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma
poorly or non-differentiated SWI/SNF and complex-deficient sinonasal carcinomas
consider for chemosensitive locally advanced tumours when standard treatment carries high morbidity
resectable stage III–IV disease
